recent_posts.title: Introducing the Theta Pulse Subchain: Powering Transparency across EdgeCloud Network
recent_posts.summary: Theta Network launches TPulse, a specialized blockchain subchain designed to track and verify AI interactions across its EdgeCloud platform. The subchain records every user engagement with AI agents—from chat messages to video views—as cryptographically verifiable transactions, solving transparency issues in centralized analytics. Major sports brands like the Vegas Golden Knights and Houston Rockets already use EdgeCloud AI agents that generate hundreds of thousands of daily interactions. TPulse enables verifiable engagement metrics, transparent compute usage tracking, and new economic models for loyalty programs, NFT platforms, and advertisers. The subchain launches with one-third of partner implementations, scaling to record AI token usage, trivia answers, video views, and e-commerce transactions as on-chain events.

recent_posts.title: AI personas create friction and break trust in user interfaces
recent_posts.summary: AI personas with names and personalities create a fragile illusion that ultimately breaks user trust. Companies anthropomorphize AI assistants to exploit human bias, but this approach adds friction to simple tasks and feels manipulative when the illusion fails. Better AI design focuses on transparency, functionality, and user control rather than fake friendliness. Personas only make sense when social interaction is the actual goal, not when users simply want to complete tasks efficiently. The best tools don't need charm or personalities—they need to work flawlessly and empower users.

recent_posts.title: Rich and dynamic user interfaces with Flutter and generative UI
recent_posts.summary: Flutter introduces GenUI SDK in alpha, enabling developers to build dynamic, personalized user interfaces generated by AI models like Gemini. The SDK orchestrates communication between users, Flutter widgets, and AI agents to transform text conversations into interactive experiences. It uses the A2UI protocol for serialization and supports multiple content generators including Google Gemini API, Firebase AI, and custom adapters. The SDK maintains brand consistency while allowing AI to compose UI from custom widget catalogs. Future plans include ADK integration, progressive rendering, full-screen composition, and Dart bytecode for server-driven UI.

recent_posts.title: “Human-Centric” API Design in the World where “AI writes the Code”
recent_posts.summary: Explores how API design must evolve in the age of AI-assisted development. Argues that while AI tools can generate code and scaffolding, thoughtful API design centered on human empathy remains critical. Emphasizes that APIs should be designed for both human developers and AI agents, with clear semantics, meaningful feedback, self-describing endpoints, and contextual examples. Inconsistent or poorly designed APIs compound problems when developers use AI code generation, making debugging more time-consuming than the time saved.

recent_posts.title: The 12th Anomaly of 3I/ATLAS: Orientation of the Jets is Not Smeared by Rotation
recent_posts.summary: Analysis of the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS reveals a puzzling 12th anomaly: its jets remain tightly collimated across millions of kilometers despite the object's 16-hour rotation period. The jets should be smeared by rotation, but observations show they maintain orientation in multiple directions. Possible explanations include rotation slowdown (unlikely), angle-dependent ice sublimation, fragment trails, or technological thrusters. This adds to 11 other anomalies including unusual trajectory alignment, composition (high nickel, low water), extreme polarization, and non-gravitational acceleration. The author maintains a wait-and-see approach on the Loeb Scale ranking pending additional data on jet speed, composition, and mass flux.

recent_posts.title: How to simplify State and Entity mappings with Kotlin interfaces, delegation and covariant generics
recent_posts.summary: Explores three approaches to managing state and data mapping in Android ViewModels with Jetpack Compose. Compares traditional data class patterns against an interface-based solution using Kotlin delegation and covariant generics. The interface approach eliminates boilerplate by allowing UiBook to implement Book through delegation, simplifying bidirectional mapping between layers. Demonstrates how private state implementations with public interfaces maintain encapsulation while reducing complexity in multi-selection scenarios and state updates.

recent_posts.title: 10 psychology principles for better UI/UX design
recent_posts.summary: Explores 10 fundamental psychology principles that influence user behavior in digital interfaces. Covers Hick's Law (limiting choices), Mere Exposure Effect (familiarity), Fitts's Law (target sizing), Aesthetic-Usability Effect (visual appeal), Serial Position Effect (placement matters), Jakob's Law (consistency), Von Restorff Effect (differentiation), Cognitive Load (simplicity), Peak-End Rule (memorable moments), and Social Proof (validation). Each principle includes practical examples from companies like Google, Instagram, Zoom, Tesla, Spotify, and Airbnb, demonstrating how understanding human behavior creates more intuitive and effective user experiences.

recent_posts.title: Fixing YouTube Playback in Jetpack Compose: The 3 Changes That Brought My Player Back
recent_posts.summary: A YouTube player integration in a Jetpack Compose app stopped working after YouTube API changes. The fix required three steps: upgrading the android-youtube-player library from 12.1.0 to 13.0.0, explicitly initializing the IFrame with IFramePlayerOptions instead of using automatic initialization, and preventing Activity recreation during rotation by adding configChanges to the manifest. These changes eliminated black screens, rotation flashes, and playback instability while simplifying the codebase by 50 lines.

recent_posts.title: Building from the Sand Up: Notes from a One-Man Orchestra
recent_posts.summary: A product designer shares their experience joining a skeletal Beijing-based automotive startup, where they juggle multiple roles from design to development while working mostly alone in an empty office. The piece explores the challenges of wearing many hats, managing conflicting visions from four different bosses, and finding authentic ownership in a resource-constrained environment. Despite the chaos of scattered remote teams, tight deadlines, and constant pivots, the author finds meaning in the direct connection between their work and tangible product impact.

recent_posts.title: As the Government Shutdown Ends, Can NASA Please Release the 40-Day-Old HiRISE Images of 3I/ATLAS?
recent_posts.summary: Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb calls for NASA to release HiRISE camera images of interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, taken 40 days ago by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter during a government shutdown. The object displays unusual characteristics including seven jets that challenge conventional comet classification. Loeb advocates for data-driven investigation over expert assumptions, announces a bet on finding extraterrestrial technological artifacts by 2030, and discusses upcoming observation opportunities as 3I/ATLAS approaches Earth in December 2025.
